summary: The main risks are the server’s lack of a checkout, transport lifecycle, authentication/attribution semantics, and incomplete bulk/sync contracts. The existing MCP transport and client provide substantial reusable infrastructure, but several seams need explicit contracts before implementation.

suggestions.title: Make structural reads snapshot-backed on the server
suggestions.rationale: StructuralService hashes repository files, rescans changed paths, removes missing slices, and reads source bytes from its root. A server without a checkout would treat persisted pages as stale or missing and cannot satisfy include_source. Add an explicit rootless mode that disables read repair and source reads, or define a server-side source snapshot capability; document the resulting tool behavior.

suggestions.title: Introduce an async server runtime with explicit resource ownership
suggestions.rationale: The current factory performs synchronous setup through transient event loops, while the HTTP transport owns sessions but does not own or close wiki and ledger stores. A long-lived HTTP process should initialize all stores in the aiohttp lifecycle, retain them for the serving loop, and close them during cleanup. Reusing the stdio factory directly risks loop affinity and leaked connections.

suggestions.title: Define static bearer authentication independently of existing API-key auth
suggestions.rationale: MCPServerConfig’s API-key path expects a configured header such as X-API-Key, while its bearer path delegates to navigator authentication rather than comparing one static environment token. Implement and test one precise Authorization: Bearer extractor with constant-time comparison, protection for POST/GET/DELETE and info endpoints, and fail-closed startup when the token is absent.

suggestions.title: Separate authenticated principal identity from X-Wiki-Actor
suggestions.rationale: The current wiki and ledger tools hardcode agent:mcp, while accepting an arbitrary trusted X-Wiki-Actor would let any bearer-token holder impersonate another human. Bind writes to the authenticated token principal, or explicitly classify the header as advisory metadata and audit both identities. If a ContextVar is used, set and reset it around every dispatch so concurrent requests cannot inherit attribution.

suggestions.title: Extend the existing HTTP session instead of adding a second client
suggestions.rationale: HttpMCPSession already parses JSON and SSE, negotiates sessions, and supports configurable headers, but notification requests do not consistently carry authentication/configured headers and request handling is stricter than the transport’s 202/204 semantics. Fix the shared header/status path and preserve structured tool errors. Do not automatically replay non-idempotent calls after session expiry; require an idempotency key or surface a retry decision.

suggestions.title: Make multi-worker session storage an explicit deployment contract
suggestions.rationale: The Streamable HTTP implementation stores sessions and resumable events in process memory, while the repository already provides RedisSessionStore specifically for cross-worker visibility and fail-closed behavior. The server must either enforce one worker, require a shared SessionStore for production, or document sticky routing; add a startup/configuration check so a multi-worker deployment cannot silently lose sessions.

suggestions.title: Create a rootless per-wiki server configuration model
suggestions.rationale: WikiProjectConfig currently derives storage and ledger paths from a repository root, and LedgerService.from_root also assumes shared-root conventions. A standalone host needs an explicit mapping of URL-safe wiki name to backend, database, ledger directory, namespaces, and structural capabilities, without calling find_shared_root or reading an absent checkout. Validate decoded path names and normalized duplicate routes before mounting.

suggestions.title: Use source-slice manifests and an atomic bulk-ingest commit
suggestions.rationale: The SQLite replacement API expresses a source-slice transaction, but ArangoDB’s implementation performs multiple delete and insert operations without one cross-operation transaction. page_hashes alone also cannot represent deleted pages or an incomplete upload, and the default upsert_symbols implementation is a no-op for backends without native symbol tables. Require source_id plus a complete slice manifest, bounded chunks, an idempotency key, an explicit commit marker, and either backend transactions or staging-and-swap; specify whether embeddings are transferred or recomputed.

suggestions.title: Treat sync push/pull as a versioned exchange protocol or defer it
suggestions.rationale: The existing sync engine operates on two BaseWikiStore instances, performs per-record LWW updates, lacks a cursor/watermark protocol, and does not provide a complete deletion/conflict exchange. A server-side wrapper cannot run it unchanged. Define paginated records and edges, timestamps, tombstones, cursors, conflict results, and resumable atomic batches; otherwise ship ingest first and keep sync remote support out of this feature.

suggestions.title: Resolve remote mode before every local store or build gate
suggestions.rationale: CLI commands currently resolve project configuration, check is_built, and open stores through local/backend-specific paths. A remote resolver added inside individual commands will miss early checks and can accidentally open ArangoDB. Centralize mode resolution before command dispatch, reject unsupported local-only flags deterministically, and define a separate local staging/cache path for build/upsert/ingest so remote mode never changes their scan semantics.

suggestions.title: Freeze command-to-tool schemas and output compatibility with contract tests
suggestions.rationale: The current tool surface is assembled dynamically, includes optional vault tools, and does not map one-to-one to rich CLI commands such as status, build, and sync. “Same output” is not guaranteed by forwarding a tools/call result. Add a versioned capability manifest, golden tests for each supported command and renderer, explicit unsupported-command errors, and interop tests using the official client for JSON and SSE responses.

suggestions.title: Keep the server dependency as a separate optional lane and make installers ownership-aware
suggestions.rationale: Core deliberately lazy-loads server-side MCP exports, and ai-parrot-server already depends on core, so making the server a normal core dependency risks a dependency cycle and bloated client installs. Add a dedicated server extra or distribution with an actionable missing-dependency error. Update Claude and Codex installers to emit HTTP entries only when configured, preserve stdio compatibility, and avoid clobbering a foreign wikitoolkit entry; test token environment wiring and Codex’s native-header limitations.
